spec_match.rationale: The model implements exactly the strict-ordering sentence (highest sendOrder drains first within a group, FIFO for ties, implementation-defined fairness across groups rendered as round-robin and labelled as such), and the code-path section shows the real API the model stands in for.

interactive.rationale: Queue-frame, queue-sync, drain, and reset buttons drive the model; queues render in drain order with sendOrder badges and the wire log explains every pick.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises the explainer's use cases in a labelled model behind a real capability probe; the page opens with that probe and the model badge.

edge_cases.rationale: Empty-drain, tie-ordering (FIFO within sendOrder 0 blobs), and the stale-frame-skipping property are all reachable and explained; the probe distinguishes no-WebTransport, pre-153, and native-capable builds.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus, the strict-ordering spec definition, and explainer §8.

conformance.rationale: The suite's manual lane/stats assertions pin the on-wire half this model illustrates; the executable surface assertions pin the probe. 0 pass / 8 fail / 2 blocked honest on Chromium 141.

runtime_evidence.rationale: The page's own contract — probe plus model — is fully executable here: headless Chromium 141 via the repo CDP harness (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this environment) drove 3 frames + 1 blob + 3 drains on desktop 1280×900 and a shorter sequence on mobile 360×740; wire order came out frame-3, state-1, frame-2 with frame-1 still queued — exactly the rule — with 0px overflow and zero failed requests on both classes. The native path is probed and reported, not simulated.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts the probe result and each drain pick; model state is local and reset is clean.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables only; media/sync wire entries use accent-blue/emerald on paper; the model badge is black-on-ivory; buttons set both colors.

accessibility.rationale: Queues and the wire are semantic lists (the wire an ordered list), every item carries sendOrder text, the explanation is one polite region updated per action, and all controls are native 44px buttons.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Driven at both classes with 0px horizontal overflow; the group grid stacks at 360px; both screenshots read.

openQuestions.title: Pair the model with a native run when an endpoint exists
openQuestions.detail: On a 153+ build with any reachable HTTP/3 WebTransport echo server, add a native run that creates the two groups and streams for real and compares observed arrival order against the model's prediction.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible live region status readout for async API probe result
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: One polite region per surface, updated with meaningful text per user action.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The explanation output is the single live region, written once per queue/drain action with the reasoning for that pick; lists are static semantic markup.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive two-panel lane layout stacking on mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: auto-fit minmax grids so paired queue panels stack on narrow viewports.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The two group panels use repeat(auto-fit, minmax(240px,1fr)); verified stacked at 360px with 0px overflow.

summary: The spec's strict-ordering rule as an interactive, honestly-labelled model behind a real capability probe, running the explainer's video-frames and bandwidth-groups scenes. Verified with the repo headless-Chromium CDP harness (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud environment) on Chromium 141: drain order matched the rule exactly, clean console/network, 0px overflow both classes.
